newsitem.title: BELGIUM: End-of-account selling undermines Brussels stocks.
newsitem.headline: End-of-account selling undermines Brussels stocks.

text.p: Light end-of-account profit-taking selling undercut the Brussels bourse in thin volume on Friday, but traders said the market remained generally well orientated.
"It is the end of the account, so people are taking profits," one trader said. "But really nothing is going on. Less than one billion francs of business has been done."
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares was 6.09 points or 0.24 percent lower at 2,575.49 at 0910 GMT, with 10 losers, three unchanged and seven gainers.

"The only issue worth mentioning is Union Miniere, which is recouping the losses of last week as the pressure of the secondary placing fades and due to the strong dollar and zinc prices," one trader said.
The non-ferrous metals firm's share price was 2.1 percent higher at 3,440 francs, making it one of the market's leading lights.
Other dollar sensitive shares such as chemical firm Solvay and banks BBL and Kredietbank also swam against the generally mild downtrend to clock up light gains.
On the negative side, chemical and pharmaceutical firm UCB stood out.
The company, which will be the first of the big firms to do so when it reports half year figures next week, was down 1.4 percent to 141,600 francs.
However, traders said the background buzz for the share remained strongly positive.

They said it was hard to determine which way the market would move when the new two-week account period opens on Monday, but noted that the release of U.S. durable goods orders later on Friday would be a strong influence.
